edges.description: Gliadin challenge of duodenal biopsies from patients in remission raises IL-17A output from mucosal CD4+ and CD4+CD8+ cells, so the gluten-driven T-cell activation node feeds the mucosal cytokine node directly.

The mixed effector cytokine response is the proximal output of gluten-specific T-cell activation that precedes intraepithelial lymphocyte cytotoxicity and villous atrophy. The intermediate steps between individual cytokines and enterocyte killing are not resolved in human tissue, so the edge is recorded as indirect.

Villous atrophy is the histologic expression of this node: cytotoxic killing of enterocytes with crypt hyperplasia shortens the villi, which is what the biopsy reports as a reduced villus-height to crypt-depth ratio.
Enterocyte loss and villous shortening reduce the absorptive surface area and the brush-border transport capacity of the proximal small intestine, which is the proximate cause of malabsorption.

Sustained IL-15-rich mucosal signaling in a chronically injured epithelium selects for intraepithelial lymphocyte clones that lose normal dependence on their activating signals. The selection pressure is inferred from the clinical sequence (uncomplicated disease preceding refractory disease type II) rather than demonstrated prospectively, so the edge is indirect.

Unabsorbed solute raises the luminal osmotic load, fat and bile salts reaching the colon are converted by bacteria into cathartic hydroxy-fatty acids, and electrolyte secretion increases; together these raise stool water. The individual contributions of the osmotic, fatty-acid, bile-acid and secretory routes have not been partitioned in celiac cohorts, so the edge is recorded as indirect.

Macronutrient malabsorption and steatorrhea create a negative energy balance. Reduced intake and inflammatory anorexia contribute in parallel and have not been separated from the absorptive loss, and a normal or raised body mass index does not exclude active disease.

Iron is absorbed principally in the proximal duodenum, which is the segment celiac disease destroys, so iron malabsorption and store depletion follow directly from the lesion's location. Menstrual or occult blood loss and inflammatory hepcidin-mediated restriction can coexist.

Fat malabsorption and reduced absorptive area impair uptake of the fat-soluble vitamins, vitamin D among them. Low dietary intake and limited sunlight exposure contribute independently, and deficiency can persist on a gluten-free diet.

Chronic energy, protein and micronutrient malabsorption in a growing child produces malnutrition and impaired weight gain, and malnutrition with chronic inflammation suppresses the growth-hormone/IGF-1 axis. The endocrine step is inferred rather than demonstrated in celiac cohorts, and socioeconomic nutrition and diagnostic delay modify the outcome, so the edge is indirect.

Short stature is the accumulated outcome of the same growth-failure branch once reduced linear growth velocity has persisted. Familial short stature, endocrine disease and failure of catch-up growth after treatment are separate explanations that this edge does not displace.
Calcium and vitamin D malabsorption lowers serum calcium and 25-hydroxy vitamin D, which raises parathyroid hormone secretion - the compensatory response that then drives skeletal resorption.
Parathyroid-hormone-driven osteoclastic resorption, together with impaired mineralization from the calcium and vitamin D deficit itself, lowers bone mineral density.

Sustained remodeling imbalance carries low bone mineral density through to osteoporosis and fragility. Age, sex hormones, low body mass index and primary osteoporosis modify the threshold, and bone density does not always normalize on a gluten-free diet, so the edge is indirect.

Clones carrying JAK1/STAT3 gain-of-function lesions, with cooperating NF-kB and epigenetic changes, expand to overt enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma. JAK1 inhibition blocked survival and proliferation of malignant refractory-disease cells in vitro, which is direct functional support for the driver role of this step. Some lymphomas arise without a recognized refractory-disease stage, and other small-intestinal lymphomas have different causal wiring.

The humoral response spreads from TG2 to the related epidermal enzyme transglutaminase 3 (TG3), and patients with dermatitis herpetiformis carry an antibody population specific for TG3 with markedly higher avidity for it than for TG2. The granular IgA precipitates that define the skin lesion contain TG3, so the antigen and the deposit are established. The terminal sequence - immune-complex deposition in dermal papillae, complement and endothelial activation, neutrophil recruitment and protease-mediated injury at the dermal-epidermal junction - is the part not fully demonstrated, and dermal IgA deposits can occur without clinical disease, so the edge is recorded as indirect.

Anti-TG2 antibodies from untreated patients bind TG2 on the maternal-facing syncytiotrophoblast and inhibit its local activity, and in primary human trophoblasts they reduce invasiveness and matrix metalloprotease activity and increase apoptosis — the proposed route from the humoral arm to impaired implantation and placentation. Epidemiologically, the excess of adverse reproductive outcomes is confined to undiagnosed disease and attenuates after diagnosis and gluten-free diet, tying the phenotype to disease activity. Mechanism attribution remains contested: malabsorption-related nutrient deficiency and systemic inflammation are credible parallel contributors, and the antibody evidence is from human tissue and cell systems with no in vivo perturbation in women, so the edge is recorded as indirect. How much weight that tissue-level and cell-level work can carry is itself unsettled in the literature, which is why the chain is placed no more strongly than indirect.

Reversible hepatocellular injury ("celiac hepatitis") is present in roughly a third to two-fifths of untreated patients and normalizes on a gluten-free diet in the large majority, so the hepatic injury tracks gluten-driven intestinal disease activity. The leading proposed route is the gut-liver axis: increased intestinal permeability delivering microbial products, antigens and cytokines to the liver through the portal circulation. The responsible portal mediator has not been identified in patients, and anti-TG2 deposition and systemic cytokines remain alternative contributors, so the edge is recorded as indirect.
Gluten ingestion is the necessary environmental trigger for the immune response against deamidated gliadin peptides in HLA-DQ2/DQ8 carriers.
Wheat is one of the three grains whose gluten storage proteins trigger and maintain the enteropathy.
Barley is one of the three grains whose gluten storage proteins trigger and maintain the enteropathy.
Rye is one of the three grains whose gluten storage proteins trigger and maintain the enteropathy.

Gluten remains the necessary trigger; enteric infection is proposed to raise the chance that a genetically susceptible person loses tolerance to it. It contributes rather than causes, which is why this is predisposing.

Targets the entry's own dysbiosis node rather than the gluten trigger. MODULATES rather than PREDISPOSES because the direction of causation here is genuinely unsettled: dysbiosis is both a proposed contributor to loss of tolerance and a consequence of established disease, and the cited source describes the microbiome as a modulator rather than a risk factor.

nodes.description: Chronic IL-15-rich signaling in the damaged epithelium selects intraepithelial lymphocyte clones that acquire JAK1 and STAT3 gain-of-function mutations, giving them cytokine-independent survival and proliferative fitness. The clinical counterpart is refractory celiac disease type II, a low-grade clonal intraepithelial lymphoproliferation that commonly precedes enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma. This is the mechanism through which the neoplastic risk of celiac disease is realized, and it is also why the risk is concentrated in patients whose mucosa does not heal.

nodes.description: Loss of absorptive surface area and brush-border transport capacity in the proximal small intestine produces defective mucosal absorption of macronutrients, iron, folate, vitamin B12, zinc and the fat-soluble vitamins. This is the convergence point through which most of the non-gastrointestinal manifestations of celiac disease are produced: it is the node the nutrient-deficiency, growth, bone and anemia branches all pass through. Deficiencies are not proportional to histologic grade - one newly-diagnosed adult cohort found vitamin and mineral deficiencies were not associated with the degree of intestinal damage - so the magnitude of this node is not read off the biopsy.

nodes.description: The effector cytokine milieu of active celiac mucosa is not purely Th1/IFN-gamma. IL-17A and IL-21 are overproduced alongside IFN-gamma, and the IL-17A-producing CD4+ and CD4+CD8+ cells largely co-express IFN-gamma rather than forming a separate stable Th17 lineage. IL-15, the innate arm cytokine, positively regulates mucosal IL-21 production, providing a mechanistic junction between the innate and adaptive arms. Curated as cytokine complexity within the canonical response, not as an independent coequal Th17 driver.
